description:
FILED s458al (agent AL, round 15), and its SHAPE was decided by a measurement
that reversed the obvious answer.

TWO gaps, one announcement channel.

(a) `(?{code})` / `(??{code})` code blocks are STRIPPED from the pattern and
    the match runs without them -- SILENTLY.  `1 while /b(?{$foo = $_})c/g`
    leaves $foo undef and says nothing; docs/not-supported.md "Regex code
    blocks".  This is the #138 family inside a regex.

(b) The CONTROL VERBS are not stripped at all, so they reach cl-ppcre:

        $_ = "aaabaaab";
        1 while /(a+b?)(*SKIP)(?{$count++; push @res,$1})(*FAIL)/g;
        # perl: count=2, res="aaab aaab"
        # PCL:  warning: Regex syntax error: Quantifier '*' not allowed. at
        #       position 7 in string "(a+b?)(*SKIP)(*FAIL)"
        #       count=0, res=

    Loud, but in cl-ppcre's words, naming a position in a pattern the program
    never wrote (the code block has already been stripped), and with no
    not-supported.md section of its own.  t/re/pat_advanced.t lines
    1235/1255/1267/1285 are the sites; they were census DROPS until #872 and
    are now honest failures.

WHY COMPILE TIME, MEASURED -- do not re-try the run-time version.  s458al
implemented the obvious fix, a `format *error-output*` in
`%pcl-strip-regex-code-blocks`, gated to fire once per pattern.  Gate green,
but the FULL SWEEP rejected it: `perl-tests/split.t` lost FOUR passing rows
(178 -> 174, "Still LOST after a serial re-run -- NOT load noise").  Those rows
are `fresh_perl_is('my @ary; @ary = split(/\w(?{ undef @ary })/, "abc");', '')`
and three siblings: the child asserts EMPTY output, so ANY stderr line makes
them fail permanently and, worse, unable ever again to detect the crash they
exist to catch.  That is a coverage LOSS, not the exposure of a row passing on
nothing.

So the announcement belongs in the `PCL:` channel the #339 drop announcer
already uses, emitted when the COMPILER sees the pattern, where no row's output
captures it.  A literal regex carries its text at compile time, which is the
whole population that matters; an interpolated pattern whose block appears only
at run time is out of reach and should stay silent rather than reintroduce the
run-time channel.

SIZING: every `(?{` in the six census populations is in perl's own regex tests
plus six `perl-tests/` files (pos.t, blocks.t, split.t, pack.t, study.t,
index.t) -- ZERO CPAN modules, measured s458al.  That is what makes the silence
affordable until this lands.

DESIGN QUESTION for the verbs: `(*FAIL)` must NOT be stripped -- dropping it
INVERTS the match's meaning -- while `(*MARK:name)` is inert without `(*SKIP)`.
So "announce and leave them to fail" is probably right for the verbs and
"announce and strip" stays right for the code blocks.

BAR: t/re/pat.t and t/re/pat_advanced.t (the sites) plus a FULL SWEEP -- the
run-time attempt was gate-green and sweep-red, so the gate alone is not the
bar.  Guard: Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t's #874 row currently asserts the strip
says NOTHING at run time; when this lands, that assertion changes to "says it
at compile time" and its companion (the statement runs, $foo undef) must not
change.


DONE s459an (agent AN, round 16), in the shape the task's own measurement dictated.  Pl::Parser::_announce_regex_gaps -- ONE pass over the document's regex tokens, called from _ppi_parse and deliberately NOT one of the three in-place repair passes, so fragment_doc's re-parses cannot double-announce.  Message `PCL: regex <what> at FILE line N -- <effect>`, a DIFFERENT verb from `PCL: statement dropped at` because the runners and gate-set-scan key on that fixed prefix and a regex gap is not a dropped statement (the statement runs; the pattern is poorer).  Gated exactly like the drop announcer, so --module is silent.  The two constructs keep OPPOSITE treatment, each for one reason: a (?{code}) block is STRIPPED (cl-ppcre has no mid-match callback) and a control verb is NOT (removing (*FAIL) would INVERT the match), so the verb reaches cl-ppcre and is rejected in cl-ppcre's words -- which is exactly what the compile-time line is there to explain.  LITERAL patterns only; a pattern built at run time from an interpolated variable stays silent rather than reintroducing the rejected channel.  BAR MET: sweep GATE clean TOTAL 18340 (+0) where the run-time attempt cost split.t four rows; corpus-diff identical 111 + 6 shapes; emission A/B vs base SAME over perl's own t/ 605 files RCDIFF 0; companion --dir re 80 files with only re/regexp_qr_embed_thr.t differing (a threads TIMEOUT the runner itself flags unstable).  re/pat_advanced.t (the (*SKIP)/(*FAIL) sites) re-run ALONE uncapped: 951/729 vs a snapshot of 673/223 -- that is #872's move from the PREVIOUS session, whose row was never refreshed because the file is quick-capped; the 605-file emission A/B proves this batch emits byte-identical CL for it.  Guard Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t +3 rows; the 'says nothing AT RUN TIME' assertion is KEPT, not weakened.  Two docs/not-supported.md sections (the code-block one updated, a new 'Regex control verbs').
subject: Announce the regex features PCL strips or cannot run -- (?{code}) blocks and the (*SKIP)/(*FAIL) control verbs -- AT COMPILE TIME
